messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] ERGM: Error in rbind (using edgecov term)‏
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I'm getting an error trying to fit an ERGM with an edgecov term, and I'm
not quite sure what it means. The error appears right after the first mcmle
iteration, in this manner:

Observed statistic(s) edgecov.del are at their greatest attainable
values. Their coefficients will be fixed at +Inf.Starting maximum
likelihood estimation via MCMLE:Iteration 1 of at most 20:Error in
rbind(if (!is.null(x2)) t(gamma * t(x2crs) + (1 - margin * gamma) *  :
  object 'm2crs' not found


This is the ERGM I was trying to model:

ergm.fit <- ergm (netdel ~ edges + mutual + nodematch("UserLevelCat")+
                  + nodecov("authorship")+                   +
nodecov("cen_degree")+                   + edgecov(fullnet, "del")


As you see, it includes several terms, but only edgecov causes a problem.
You may have noticed that the network I use for the edgecov term is
different than the main one, and this is since *netdel *is the binary
version of *fullnet, *which consists valued edges.

Any help would be appreciated!

Thanks in advance,
Ben Fargeon
Ben-Gurion University of the Negev

messages.body_plain:
Hi Ben -

If I understand correctly, netdel is a binary network that has a 0 
everywhere fullnet has a 0, and has a 1 everywhere that fullnet has a 
value >1.? Is that right?? If so, then you can't really use fullnet as a 
predictor of whether or not there is a tie in netdel, as there will be 
collinearity between the two.? The error you got is not very clear, I 
realize, but I do suspect that that is the underlying problem. Can you 
clarify (off group if you wish) what it is you are aiming to show by 
having fullnet as a predictor of netdel?? Knowing that may help to 
figure out what would be an appropriate analysis. Depending on the 
answer, one good option may be to use valued ergms with fullnet as your 
outcome. See the valued ergm tutorial at: 
https://statnet.org/trac/wiki/Sunbelt2016.

HTH,

Steve
